To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the atomic structure of the MAP Kinase ERK2 has been determined to a resolution of two angstroms, and that the structure of the enzyme in its unphophorylated, low-activity conforation is significantly different from that in its active, phosphorylated conformation.

the atomic structure of the mitogen-activated protein kinase, ERK2, has been determined in its unphosporylated low-activty conformation to a high resolution of 2 Angstroms and the two domains are far apart and the peptide-binding region is blocked by tyosine 185, which is one of the two sites that become phosphorylated when the enzyme is activated by Ras and Raf.
the atomic structure of the unphosphorylatable low-activity form of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAP kinase) ERK2 has been determined by x-ray crystallography at a resolution of 0.23 nm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and mechanism of protein kinases, and in particular, with the mitogen-activated protein kinases (MAPKs).
the structure of the MAP kinases, which are key regulators in the Ras-Raf-ERK signal transduction cascade.
the molecular basis of the activation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase ERK2 and with the role of ERK2 in the regulation of gene transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents the first high-resolution structure of an unphosphoryated MAP kinase, and that the structure is consistent with the known biochemical and mutagenesis data for the ERK family of MAP kinases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of the unphosphoryated form of ERK2, the most active kinase in the human genome, is solved at 2.2 Å resolution and the structure of ERK2 bound to the peptide substrate, a peptide derived from the transcription factor Elk-1, is solved at the same resolution.
the structure of unphosphoylated ERK2 is a snapshot of the conformation of the enzyme that is not capable of binding substrate.
the structure of ERK2 reveals a novel mechanism of protein kinase regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of unphosphorlylated ERK2, which is the inactive form of this enzyme, is very different from the structure of the active form.
ERK2 has a very different conformation from that of the active conformation in PKA.
the activation of MAP kinases involves a global conformational change, not just local changes in the peptide-binding site, and that the activation loop is a key element in the conformational change.
